title: Sasando (Rote tube zither)
summary: The sasando is a tube zither from the island of Rote in eastern Indonesia. A bamboo tube is wrapped with strings and stands inside a fan-shaped bowl of dried palm leaf, which lends the plucked notes a bright, shimmering ring.
howToPlay: Look at the tube: the strings run around it, low notes on one side and high notes on the other.
Watch a bead travel down each string toward its wooden wedge.
Pluck the string just as the bead arrives.
Play the lullaby first, then the livelier gathering step.
rules: The strings are tuned to a seven-note scale, with wooden wedges setting each pitch.
A pluck right on the beat is perfect and a close one is good.
Extra plucks that match no note cost points.
Each tune is played through twice.
heritageNote: The sasando belongs to the island of Rote and nearby islands in eastern Indonesia, where makers shape the tube, wedges and palm-leaf bowl by hand. Players pluck both sides of the tube with the fingertips, and the instrument is still made and played today.
